sections: 1. c) Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) — executes the instruction's operation (the CU directs it).
2. b) RAM — volatile; loses contents without power.
3. c) Directs the flow of data and instructions.
4. a) Executing multiple instructions simultaneously in a sequence of stages.
2. FALSE — RAM is volatile; ROM/Flash are non-volatile.
5. FALSE — the CU controls; it does not store data permanently.

Beyond 8 cores: no significant gains — the maximum theoretical speedup with infinitely many cores is 1/0.30 ≈ 3.33×, so moving from 8 → ∞ cores gains only ~0.75× more; the 30% sequential portion dominates.

Strategy for the sequential part: optimize that code itself (better algorithm, faster single-core path), or boost single-thread performance (higher clock, more cache, ILP); alternatively restructure the workload to shrink the serial fraction (e.g. parallelize parts of Task B, pipeline it with Task A).
